best_for: People and small teams who keep the same files on two or three computers and want them synced without thinking, and who will pay once 2 GB runs out.
description:
Dropbox is a cloud storage and file sync service from Dropbox, Inc., which Drew Houston co-founded in 2007 to make keeping files in sync simpler. The desktop app puts a Dropbox folder on your computer, and every change you make there shows up on dropbox.com and on your phone and tablet.

Right-click a file in that folder to see its version history or send it out for a signature. Share a link to photos, videos, zipped folders or CAD files with anyone, even people without a Dropbox account, and control how much each person can do. Click the Dropbox icon in the taskbar or menu bar to search your files and see recent activity. You can also back up folders such as your Desktop.

points.title: The free plan is small
points.text: Dropbox Basic is free and gives 2 GB of storage. You need a Dropbox account to use the app at all, so plan on signing in during setup.

points.title: Three devices on Basic
points.text: A free account can be signed in on three computers or phones at once. Adding a fourth means signing out of one or upgrading. Signing in on dropbox.com in a browser does not count toward the limit.

points.title: Paid plans start at Plus
points.text: Plus is listed at USD 9.99 per month for one person with 2 TB, unlimited devices, 30 days of file recovery and transfers up to 50 GB. Standard for teams is USD 15 per user per month and starts at 3 TB with 180 days of recovery. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Where the desktop app will not run
points.text: Windows needs 10 or 11 on an NTFS drive, and S mode and Windows Server are not supported. On a Mac, macOS 11 or later gets the full app, while 10.13 to 10.15 get a simpler version.

points.title: Linux is narrower
points.text: Dropbox supports 64-bit Ubuntu 18.04 or later and Fedora 28 or later, on x64 only. Other distributions may work but are not supported. The Flatpak here is a Flathub package that Flathub does not mark as verified, and it trails the Windows and Mac builds by a few versions.

points.title: Windows keeps a long history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 200 versions, as .exe and MSI installers for x86, x64 and Arm64 that install for all users. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
